advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Move the `--report-exit` guard before the IMDS prologue (fetch REGION only within the guard) so the truncation hook is minimal and does not depend on a prologue that runs under the pressure it reports on.
evidence: lines 140-145 fetch TOKEN/REGION/IID via curl BEFORE the guard
observability.sh:165 `if [ "${1:-}" = "--report-exit" ]; then`
observability.sh:169-170 `aws cloudwatch put-metric-data --region "$REGION" ... --metric-name probe_truncated ... 2>/dev/null || true`
The truncation signal's own publication depends on a REGION fetch that runs under the failure conditions it reports on; its failure is invisible.
advisory.finding: The `--report-exit` (ExecStopPost) guard is placed AFTER the three IMDSv2 curls (TOKEN/REGION/IID at lines 140-145), so every stop — including every successful oneshot completion — re-executes the prologue and issues up to 3 IMDS requests (each `--max-time 5`) before the guard at line 165 exits. On the truncated-run path this hook is meant to be minimal, and if REGION cannot be fetched under the same pressure that truncated the run, `probe_truncated` is published with an empty `--region` and the PutMetricData silently fails (`2>/dev/null || true`), so the truncation death certificate itself can be lost exactly when it is needed.
advisory.suggested_fix: Hoist the `--report-exit` branch above the TOKEN/REGION/IID fetch and fetch REGION inside the branch (or accept REGION from the environment) so the hook does the least possible work.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm overlay2 is on the same filesystem as $DOCKER_ROOT (or document that the overlay2 breadcrumb subtotal is best-effort under `-x`).
evidence: observability.sh:653 `out="$(clamped "$DOCKER_DU_TIMEOUT" du -x --block-size=1 --max-depth=1 "$root" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1`
awk match `$2 == root "/overlay2" { overlay = $1 }` takes whatever `du -x` emits for that child, which is a mount stub if overlay2 is a separate fs
advisory.finding: `docker_du_census` uses `du -x --max-depth=1`; when `$DOCKER_ROOT/overlay2` resides on a separate filesystem the `-x` (one-file-system) prune emits it as a mount-point stub rather than its true recursive subtotal, so `DOCKER_DU_OVERLAY2` (and the overlay2 breadcrumb) can silently under-report. This matches prior behavior for the total but the overlay2 subtotal now comes from a single `-x` walk whose semantics for a separately-mounted child differ from a dedicated `du` over that child.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the --report-exit hook resolve region from a cached/env source (or short-circuit before the IMDS curls) so probe_truncated still publishes when IMDS is unavailable.
evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh:142 `REGION=$(curl -s --max-time 5 http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/placement/region ...)`
infra/scripts/observability.sh:169-170 `aws cloudwatch put-metric-data --region "$REGION" ... --metric-name probe_truncated ... 2>/dev/null || true`
The --report-exit branch at line 165 runs only AFTER the IMDS fetch at 140-145, so a stalled/failed IMDS leaves $REGION empty and the truncation metric is lost with `|| true`.
ABSENCE: no fallback region source (e.g. AWS_REGION env or a cached region file) for the ExecStopPost path, so the death-certificate publisher shares the failure mode of the run it is reporting on.
advisory.finding: The ExecStopPost truncation-certificate hook depends on IMDS region resolution succeeding, but under I/O pressure (the exact failure this bug is about) the region curl can hang/fail; put-metric-data then runs with an empty --region and the failure is swallowed by `|| true`, so probe_truncated is silently never published in precisely the scenario it exists for.
scenarios: Host under IOPS saturation SIGTERM-ed the run AND IMDS is slow/unresponsive; the ExecStopPost hook cannot resolve region and probe_truncated is never emitted, so the probe_not_completing alarm is the only signal — reintroducing the ambiguity this change set out to remove.
advisory.suggested_fix: Move the `--report-exit` short-circuit above the IMDS fetch and source REGION from the AWS_REGION env / an at-install-time cached region file, falling back to IMDS only if unset.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit TimeoutStopSec to rebar-observability.service and/or move the --report-exit short-circuit before the IMDS curls so the stop hook cannot hang on IMDS.
evidence: infra/scripts/install-observability.sh:37 `ExecStopPost=/usr/local/bin/rebar-observability.sh --report-exit`
infra/scripts/install-observability.sh:49 `TimeoutStartSec=240` (no TimeoutStopSec set)
infra/scripts/observability.sh:140-145 three IMDS curls with `--max-time 5` run before the `--report-exit` guard at line 165
ABSENCE: no explicit TimeoutStopSec in the [Service] section to bound the ExecStopPost hook.
advisory.finding: The systemd unit sets TimeoutStartSec=240 for ExecStart but no TimeoutStopSec; the new ExecStopPost re-runs the same script which unconditionally issues three IMDS curls (up to 3x5s) before the --report-exit branch, so stop can hang up to the default TimeoutStopSec (90s) on a wedged IMDS.
scenarios: IMDS wedged during a stop transition holds the unit in deactivating state; since OnUnitActiveSec is measured from last completed activation, a slow stop erodes the same timer-liveness property TimeoutStartSec was added to protect.
advisory.suggested_fix: Set `TimeoutStopSec=30` in the [Service] block and place the `--report-exit` branch before the IMDS block in observability.sh.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the source-text grep in test_every_wall_clock_bound_goes_through_clamped with a behavioral check (a recording `timeout` stub asserting every bounded call receives a grant <= budget_left, as tests 7/8 already do for the docker walk) so the composition invariant survives a refactor.
evidence: lines = SCRIPT.read_text().splitlines()
if re.search(r'(?<![\w-])timeout "\$', line) or re.search(r"(?<![\w-])bounded \d", line):
exempt = ('bounded() { timeout "$@"; }', 'bounded "$want" "$@"')

The assertion is over the text of the implementation (SCRIPT.read_text()), not over observable behaviour; the exempt tuple hardcodes exact source lines so any reformat of `bounded`'s definition or of `clamped`'s delegation trips a false failure.
advisory.finding: test_every_wall_clock_bound_goes_through_clamped asserts over the literal source text of observability.sh (the unit under test), matching implementation strings with regexes and an exact-string exempt tuple. It is a source-grep change-detector: a behavior-preserving refactor (renaming `clamped`, reformatting `bounded() { timeout "$@"; }` onto multiple lines, or writing a clamped call across two lines) breaks the test without any observable-behavior change.
scenarios: A maintainer reformats the one-line `bounded()` definition or renames the composition helper without changing behaviour, and this test fails.
A legitimately-clamped call is wrapped across two lines, evading the regex or tripping the raw-`timeout` matcher.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen test_expensive_call_cannot_spend_the_tail_reserve to assert the granted duration (via a recording timeout stub) rather than only run completion, or fold it into test 7 which already measures the grant.
evidence: """A budget already inside the reserve clamps the next expensive call to a fail-fast 1 s."""
assert _values(probe.aws_log, "probe_ok") == ["1"]

The fixture stub `_stub(bin_dir, "timeout", 'shift\nexec "$@"')` discards the granted duration, so probe_ok=1 is emitted whether the clamp grants 1s, 100s, or is removed — the assertion is regression-blind for the stated clamping contract (the grant is only actually measured in test_clamp_hands_an_exhausted_budget_to_the_expensive_call).
advisory.finding: test_expensive_call_cannot_spend_the_tail_reserve claims to verify that an exhausted budget clamps the next expensive call to the 1s floor, but its only assertion is `_values(probe.aws_log, 'probe_ok') == ['1']` (the run completed). Under the fixture's faithful `timeout` stub (`shift; exec "$@"`), which discards the duration, the run completes regardless of whether `clamped` grants 1s or is deleted entirely — so the assertion cannot detect a regression in the clamping behaviour it names.
scenarios: A mutation that removes or breaks the clamp's floor arithmetic leaves this test green because completion, not the grant, is asserted.

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 340 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug 9313-1fac-9f32-4b07 has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix like this is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan 9313-1fac-9f32-4b07` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review 9313-1fac-9f32-4b07` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan 9313-1fac-9f32-4b07 --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm /var/lib/docker and overlay2 are on the same filesystem on all target hosts, or drop `-x` / walk the actual data-root mount, before relying on the single-walk total.
evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh: `out="$(clamped "$DOCKER_DU_TIMEOUT" du -x --block-size=1 --max-depth=1 "$root" ...)"`

The prior two-walk shape ran `du -sx "$DOCKER_ROOT/overlay2"` as its own root, so overlay2-on-a-separate-mount was still measured directly; the single `-x` walk of the root cannot cross that mount boundary.
ABSENCE: no detection/handling for overlay2 being a distinct mountpoint; the row simply does not appear and DOCKER_DU_OVERLAY2 becomes ""/'-'.
dropped.finding: docker_du_census walks with `du -x` (single filesystem); if /var/lib/docker/overlay2 (or the docker root) is a separate mount, both the grand total and the overlay2 subtotal silently exclude it, changing docker_storage_bytes / docker_unaccounted_bytes semantics without any signal.
scenarios: Hosts that mount /var/lib/docker/overlay2 (or the docker data-root) on a dedicated volume — a common production layout — will under-report docker storage after this change, shifting docker_unaccounted_bytes silently.
